title: Ethiopian Coffee
community: All of Ethiopia — everyday Ethiopian coffee
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Buna — strong coffee brewed in a clay jebena, served black in small cups with sugar on the side. The everyday version of the coffee ceremony — the morning ritual of millions of Ethiopians. With salt in Harrar, with sugar everywhere else, with butter in some highland communities.
longDesc: Ethiopian everyday coffee is the simplified ceremony — the jebena on the charcoal, the ground coffee, the patient brewing, and the small cup. It is the first thing done every morning in millions of Ethiopian homes, the punctuation mark of every social visit.
ingredients: 3 tbsp medium-coarse ground Ethiopian arabica coffee
// Optional: pinch of cardamom, pinch of salt (Harrar tradition), 1 tsp butter (highland tradition)
equipment: Jebena (clay coffee pot) or small saucepan
steps: Fill jebena with cold water. Place on flame.
When water boils, add ground coffee.
Pour slowly and from a height into sini cups — the height creates a light foam.
Serve with sugar on the side.
chefTips: Ethiopian coffee is always drunk black — no milk.
Pouring from a height is essential — aerates the coffee and creates the characteristic small foam.
The Harrar tradition of adding a pinch of salt to the cup (not the jebena) is worth trying — it reduces bitterness.
If using a saucepan: bring to a gentle boil, remove from heat, steep 5 minutes, pour through a fine sieve.
cookingScience: Jebena brewing is similar to Turkish/Ibrik coffee — the fine grounds are not filtered, allowing complete extraction of oils and all soluble compounds. This produces a coffee with significantly more body and antioxidants than paper-filtered coffee.
sustainabilityTips: Ethiopian arabica grown in shade forest systems — the most sustainable coffee on earth.
healthBenefits: Among the world's highest antioxidant coffee.
The unfiltered method retains maximum beneficial compounds.
culturalNote: Ethiopian coffee is the thread that holds Ethiopian social life together — no visit is complete without it, no morning is begun without it, no conversation is deepened without it. The small cup of strong black coffee is the most fundamental Ethiopian hospitality offering.
